utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Will the Registrar call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is case number 95-9-PT, the Prosecutor versus Simic and others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And may we have the appearances for the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Nancy Paterson representing the Office of the Prosecutor, and with me is Andrew Powell, the case manager. I'd just like to inform the Court that this will be Mr. Powell's last appearance on the case. He will be leaving the Tribunal at the end of the month.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. For the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Deyan Brashich for the Todorovic defence, and I would like to introduce to the Court my legal assistant Mr. Zivan Blagojevic of the Republika Srpska bar. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Igor Pantelic for Mr. Miroslav Tadic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Slobodan Zecevic for Milan Simic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZEREVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Aleksander Lazerevic for Mr. Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: This is a Status Conference pursuant to the provisions of Rule 65 bis. Before making the usual inquiries of the accused, I will deal with the outstanding matters and provide information on pending issues. I have listed six. First, the motion relating to requests for judicial assistance, a decision on that motion will be given shortly. Secondly, there is before the Chamber a motion filed by the accused Todorovic seeking the assistance of the Chamber in accessing documents in domestic proceedings in the FRY. Mr. Brashich, I think you were to give us some information --

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: -- as to whether you had succeeded in becoming a party to those proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I have. As I had advised the Court, Mr. Blagojevic and I have filed notices of appearance in those proceedings representing the interests of the victim, Mr. Todorovic, under the procedure as they exist in the FRY. On the 18th of October, the trial of the five accused will commence at Uzice, and I intend to appear there with Mr. Blagojevic. I have met with the Prosecution, and they will make available to me statements and transcripts -- or I guess they would be minutes of the proceedings, and at that particular time, I will withdraw my request for judicial assistance as to the FRY. I have given notice to Ms. Paterson of the proceedings, and I have also given her notice of the name of the prosecutor and the judge. I confirm now that as of this morning, notwithstanding the situation in the FRY, the proceedings will commence on the 18th, and they're scheduled to run for three days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Our next matter relates to the two motions regarding the issue of the legality of arrest. First, the request for return to the FRY, and the second, the application for habeas corpus. In relation to that, as you know, there is an ongoing evidentiary hearing. The date for the continuation of that hearing will clearly have to await the decision in the motion for the request for judicial assistance. As I said earlier, that decision will be given very shortly. It may also have to wait other matters arising out of that, that decision. The next matter is an application on behalf of the accused Tadic for an extension of provisional release in respect of medical examination. Who is the counsel? Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I am, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Do you wish that to be taken in closed or private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I don't think it's necessary, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Would you have anything to say on the motion?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just a few words. Maybe it is not so clear from our application. I spoke with Mrs. Featherstone about this issue. I just simply informed her that due to the extraordinary moments, the relevant medical experts from the clinical centre from Banja Luka were at Macedonia participating in some symposium or something, so this seven days which was agreed and which was -- sorry -- yes, permitted by the Court due to this fact was not sufficient to perform additional analysis of a neurological doctor. So simply due to this reason, we were obliged to submit our application for additional time of four days of examinations in order to complete the general examinations, medical examinations of my client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. The motion itself is quite clear. Ms. Paterson, would you have any response at this time?

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, actually, I was about to prepare a written response, and then when I realised we were going to have this session today, if it's acceptable to the Court, I'm willing to just give our oral response, which is we have no objection to Mr. Tadic getting the treatment he's requested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. The Chamber will give a decision on this early next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So a decision on that will be given early next week. The next matter is a request by the accused Todorovic for access to the OTP investigator Mr. Brondum. The stage at which this was is that I think the parties are now to confirm whether the Defence has spoken with the investigator and whether there is a need to call him. Mr. Brashich?

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: Your Honour, Ms. Paterson and I conferred on the matter.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Mr. Brashich. Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: I think that we have resolved the matter. I have been given access to the investigator by telephone. I interviewed him at length by telephone, and I do plan to call him as a witness. I am satisfied, after discussing the circumstances of the arrest, and the guidelines under which the investigator operated, that he would be a necessary witness, and he has told me that he's perfectly willing to come and testify at this Chamber's pleasure. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. The next Status Conference will have to be held sometime prior to the 8th of February, 2001, and the usual contacts will be made with a view to fixing the date. May I now inquire from the accused, Mr. Todorovic, whether there is any matter that you wish to raise in relation to your conditions of detection or indeed in relation to any other matter. THE ACCUSED TODOROVIC: [Interpretation] Mr. President, thank you for your interest. For the moment, I have nothing in particular to say. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Todorovic. There being no other matter to be raised -- Mr. Brashich, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'm mindful of the court's comments that the decision will be shortly forthcoming. I'm mindful of the tremendous case load that this Court has. However, just very briefly, I would like to place on the record that I'm pressing as hard as I can on behalf of my client to resolve the issue, and I do not wish to in any way offend the Court, I just want to make a statement that I, as the counsel for the Defence, am doing everything in my power, and I'm sure the Court is doing the same. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Brashich. I think you're acting very properly, and I'd like to assure you that the Court is very sensitive to the pressures of time, and we will see to it that the evidentiary hearing resumes at the earliest opportunity.

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The hearing is adjourned.
